phase_task.title: Hardening & FDE-Readiness: requirement gap-closure, production-grade refactor (interface-preserving), the full test taxonomy, a privileged admin console, and an FDE-grade DESIGN.md
phase_task.goal: Phases 0-9 built and verified the platform. Phase 10 makes it defensible to a reviewer and deployable by a forward-deployed engineer. It has FIVE parallel-authored but independently-gated workstreams: (A) close every requirement gap and contradiction found in the critique; (B) raise the code to production grade against DRY/SOLID and language best practice WITHOUT changing any external IO/API contract; (C) complete the eleven-layer test taxonomy to the stated coverage bar; (D) add a MASTER admin console for a single hardcoded superuser as an explicitly out-of-band privileged operator plane that does NOT breach the consumer isolation invariant; (E) rewrite DESIGN.md into a forward-deployed-engineer-friendly document that proves every requirement and adds cost, HLD/LLD, failure-modes, tradeoffs, and the FDE sections. Nothing in the plan-of-record capability set may regress.

prime_constraints.constraint: Workstreams A, B, C, E MUST NOT change any externally-observable IO contract: /v1 route shapes, request/response JSON schemas, CLI command surface, the Makefile target names, the sandbox VerificationResult shape, the model XML wire format, or the DB row schemas consumers depend on. Internal refactors (registries, base classes, extracted helpers, typed accessors, transaction consolidation) are in-scope; signature changes on public surfaces are NOT. Any finding tagged interface-affecting below is called out explicitly and must be gated behind a deliberate decision, not applied silently.

Workstream D introduces a PRIVILEGED, cross-tenant surface. This directly tensions with hard requirements #1 (API-only: index/sandbox/model unreachable by consumers) and #2 (per-user isolation by construction). It is FORBIDDEN to satisfy the admin console by adding a cross-tenant read path onto any /v1 route or onto the single published consumer port. The admin plane MUST be a separate auth realm on a separate mount/port, read-mostly, and audit-logged, and the tradeoff MUST be documented in DESIGN.md. The consumer isolation invariant and its proving tests must remain literally true and green.

The full existing suite stays green; `make up` still boots one-command, keyless, in stub mode; `make eval` still passes all >=5 tasks against their oracles. The stub model backend must never import the Anthropic SDK.
Per the persona's docs discipline, each workstream writes its DESIGN.md / ADR section in the same pass — never backfilled. Workstream E is the consolidation, not the first write.

workstream.name: Requirement gap-closure & contradiction repair
workstream.intent: Re-audit the build against execution_plan.md (§2 hard reqs #1-9, §3 adversarial #1-8, §4 doc deliverables, §5 stretch, §7 self-check) and close every gap, stub, unproven claim, and doc/code contradiction. The critique below is the seed work-list; the executing agent must re-verify each item in code before acting and add any it finds.

deliverables.d: Polyglot runners + the DESIGN/ADR contradiction. Two coupled problems: (i) §11 "What we cut" says the Phase-8 runners were not implemented while ADR-0003 documents them SHIPPED with a parity table — a self-contradicting requirement-to-proof matrix destroys reviewer trust. (ii) Ground truth is worse than a doc typo: the Go/Rust/TS entrypoints (sandbox/{go,rust,ts}) re-implement the harness but their build+test gate is STILL `python3 -m compileall` + `python3 -m pytest` on a python:3.12-slim image (main.go:157,174; main.rs:244,266; main.ts:142,154) — so "parity" is near-tautological (every runner verifies Python). FIX: either make each runner build/test its OWN language (`go test`, `cargo test`, `tsc`+`npm test`) with a per-language fixture, OR reframe ADR-0003 + DESIGN honestly as "language-diverse harness parity, Python verification core" and resolve the cut-vs-shipped contradiction. Pick one and make code+docs agree.

Correctness: loop.py `_do_verify` passes base_commit=task.workspace_id into a field contractually holding the base COMMIT. Pass self._snap.commit (already computed). Latent bug for any real conflict-detecting runner. Add a regression test asserting the verify request carries the resolved commit.

Metering dimensions never written (permanently 0). Both tasks.retrieval_bytes AND tasks.sandbox_seconds columns exist (schema.sql:55-56) and are read by the API, dashboard, and TaskStatus (tasks_router.py:124, dashboard_router.py:62-63, loop.py:744-745) — but the ONLY metering UPDATE is _bump_task_tokens (loop.py:696-703), which sets tokens/tool_calls only. Endangers Hard Req #6 (per-task metering) and #9 (per-run trace fidelity). FIX: in _do_retrieve accumulate RetrievalResult.byte_count into tasks.retrieval_bytes; in _do_verify record the sandbox result duration into tasks.sandbox_seconds. Also decide the per-step retrieval step_index tag (retrieval/service.py passes None at all six primitives): wire it through or delete the dead parameter. Add a test asserting a task with retrieval + a verify ends with non-zero retrieval_bytes and sandbox_seconds.

Remove dead/misleading code: loop.py `_replay_data_spans_with_failures` is never called and its body contradicts its docstring. Delete it (the real failure-span reconstruction lives in `_replay_effect`).

DESIGN.md §11 "Would do next" lists "Confirm pricing and wire USD stop" twice (#1 and #3) — dedupe. Reconcile the drifted section numbering so every one of the 18 FDE topics (workstream E) has one canonical home.

Re-run the §7 pre-submission self-check (10 items) as explicit assertions and record pass/fail with file:line evidence in the DESIGN.md coverage matrix. Any item not backed by a test is a gap to close in workstream C.

Wall-clock budget is stored but NEVER enforced. wall_clock_seconds threads to the task (service.py:60) but _budget_breach (loop.py:621-631) checks only step + token — there is no time check anywhere, so a task on a LIVE model backend can run unbounded in wall-clock. Directly breaks Hard Req #6 ("wall-clock deadline") and Adversarial #7 (budget exhausted mid-task). FIX: capture start = time.monotonic() in run() and add to _budget_breach: `if time.monotonic() - start >= task.wall_clock_seconds: return BUDGET_EXHAUSTED(reason)`, stopping at the current journaled checkpoint. Add a test with a tiny wall-clock budget + a slow stub step asserting a clean BUDGET_EXHAUSTED with partial progress and an intact worktree.

The eval harness, the walkthrough demos, and make demo-* verify against a `_FakeSandbox`, not Docker (eval/demo.py:38-55, eval/runner.py:51-91) — the verdict derives from a path/artifact match, not a real build+test. The real Docker verification exists (docker_runner.py:305, sandbox/entrypoint.py: 168-192) but is exercised ONLY by Docker-gated integration tests that skip silently when Docker is absent. This hollows the assignment's central proof ("done only after a real build + test in the sandbox", self-check #2/#10). FIX: add a real-Docker eval/demo path (e.g. `make eval-docker`, `make demo-happy SANDBOX=docker`) running the SAME oracles against DockerSandboxRunner, and make the submission proof depend on it; and make the Docker-gated tests FAIL (not skip) when the sandbox image is buildable but tests were skipped (ties to C: Docker layer). At minimum, document loudly that stub-eval uses a fake sandbox and the real proof is the Docker suite. This is the most important correctness-of-claim gap.

The concurrent-write guarantee is not wired into the apply path. commit_worktree (workspace/service.py:121-203) implements flock + base-commit-check -> ConflictError and is unit-tested, but grep shows ONLY tests call it: the loop applies edits to the worktree and terminates WITHOUT committing back through the guarded path. So Adversarial #6 ("two tasks edit same workspace concurrently -> never silent clobber") is proven in a helper that production flow never invokes. FIX: on VERIFIED_SUCCESS in APPLY mode, have the loop call commit_worktree(base_commit=handle.base_commit) and handle ConflictError (rebase-reverify or reject). Combine with the B-6 atomicity fix. Add an integration test where two concurrent APPLY tasks on one workspace resolve to exactly one commit + one ConflictError.

Per-key rate limiting is documented but entirely absent. auth.py:7 claims "per-key rate limit (sliding window counted in the DB)" and schema.sql:22 carries rate_limit_per_min, but require_auth enforces nothing — no window count, no 429, no test. A false security claim endangers Hard Req #3. FIX: implement a DB- or memory-backed sliding-window counter in require_auth returning 429 on breach (+ a test), OR, if descoped, delete the claim from the docstring and DESIGN and record the decision. Do not leave it claimed but unimplemented.

Multi-file rename uses non-scope-aware whole-file substitution (loop.py:505 `original.replace(old_name, new_name)`) — renaming `user` corrupts `user_id`, `username`, etc. Endangers Stretch #2 correctness and can ship a broken rename past a weak test suite. FIX: replace only identifier tokens using the index's reference SPANS (line/col), not raw substrings. Add the name-collision test from workstream C. (Interface- preserving; internal to _do_rename.)

workstream.oracle: Each fixed gap has a test that fails before the fix and passes after (A2, A3, A7, A9, A10, A11). Wall-clock exhaustion produces a clean BUDGET_EXHAUSTED with partial report and intact worktree (A7). A real-Docker eval/demo path runs the same oracles and the Docker suite FAILS rather than skips when the image is buildable (A8). Two concurrent APPLY tasks resolve to one commit + one ConflictError via the production path (A9). A burst past rate_limit_per_min returns 429 — or the claim is removed (A10). retrieval_bytes and sandbox_seconds are non-zero after a real run (A3). No grep hit for the dead method (A4). DESIGN.md and ADR-0003 agree on polyglot status and each runner's actual verification language is stated truthfully (A1). The §7 self-check table is present and every row cites evidence (A6). The critique is delivered as a written gap register (docs/critique.md or a DESIGN.md appendix) mapping every requirement to fulfilled / partial / missing with evidence and severity.

workstream.name: DRY / SOLID / pattern hardening — no IO change
workstream.intent: Apply targeted, interface-preserving fixes that raise the code to production grade. Prefer the language-idiomatic pattern (registry, command/strategy, repository, composition-root/DI, context-manager, thread-local/pooled connection) over ad-hoc branching. Every fix keeps the public surface byte-identical.

critical.fix: The Database facade shares ONE sqlite3.Connection (check_same_thread= False) with no lock/pool across FastAPI sync (`def`) endpoints, which Starlette runs on a threadpool. Two threads entering `immediate()` collide ("cannot start a transaction within a transaction") or one COMMIT prematurely commits another's half-written work — BEGIN IMMEDIATE only serializes across SEPARATE connections. This undermines the WAL+IMMEDIATE serialization the whole ledger/journal correctness story rests on. FIX: thread-local connection factory (or a small per-worker pool), each opened once with the same pragmas; or wrap `immediate()` and raw reads in a threading.RLock (simpler, correctness-preserving, acceptable throughput cost at demo scale). Public methods (immediate/conn/close, all repo APIs) unchanged. This is the single highest-leverage fix and gates B-* below.

high.fix: Wrap client.messages.create() and map anthropic.RateLimitError / APIStatusError / APIConnectionError / AuthenticationError onto a new typed UpstreamModelError(ACPError) (carry request_id, never the key or channel content). Today a raw SDK exception aborts the run before the journal row is written, forcing a paid re-issue on resume. Success-path ModelResponse contract unchanged.

Inspect stop_reason before joining text: raise distinct typed errors for "refusal" (empty content, HTTP 200) and "max_tokens" (truncation). Today both surface as a misleading generic "not well-formed XML" from parse_action. Only assemble XML on end_turn.

`_charge` does check-then-act over the ledger across 4+ independent transactions (remaining_tokens SELECTs, then RESERVE/COMMIT/RELEASE each in its own immediate()), despite the docstring claiming atomicity. Two concurrent retrievals on one scope can both pass the check and overshoot the budget (TOCTOU). Add LedgerRepo.charge_atomic(...) doing the SELECT SUM and the inserts under ONE BEGIN IMMEDIATE. BudgetExceeded / no-write- on-refusal semantics and RetrievalResult unchanged.

create_task injects BackgroundTasks but never uses it; submit() runs the full loop inline and blocks up to max_wall_seconds while the docstring claims async 202. Decide: (a) truly schedule via background_tasks.add_task (SSE already exists to stream progress) returning the PENDING snapshot, or (b) delete the unused param and correct the docstring to "runs to terminal before 202". Response schema/status unchanged. Note (a) changes WHICH metering snapshot is returned — pick deliberately.

Kill/OOM/network classification uses Python/glibc-flavored substring markers baked into the runner and inherited unaudited by the Go/Rust/TS polyglot subclasses — a Rust phone-home may be misclassified as an ordinary test failure, silently weakening the parity claim. Extract a unit-testable ResultParser and make the network/OOM marker set a per-runner override. SandboxClient protocol + VerificationResult unchanged.

commit_worktree's base-commit check + copytree + set_head is a read-modify-write across FS and DB not in one transaction; a crash between copytree and set_head leaves on-disk state and recorded head inconsistent, weakening the "no silent clobber" ConflictError guarantee. Make the DB the commit point: conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE head_commit=:base` inside one immediate() (rowcount==0 -> ConflictError), copy to temp + atomic rename. Keep flock as optimization. Signature/contract unchanged. NOTE: pairs with A9 — this atomicity fix is moot until the loop actually CALLS commit_worktree on apply, which A9 wires in.

Two cost calculators (dashboard hardcodes per-token constants; tasks_router reads settings price_per_1k_*). They agree numerically today but are two sources of truth flagged PLACEHOLDER. Extract one cost function (common/pricing.py or on Settings); both routers call it; delete the hardcoded pair. cost_usd field + rounding preserved.

medium.fix: AgentLoop reaches around its repos: `_committed_model_steps` runs raw SQL with a `note LIKE 'model:%'` string that belongs in LedgerRepo; and json.loads(payload_json) with scattered .get() defaults is repeated in 7+ methods. Add LedgerRepo.committed_step_indices(scope, task_id) and a typed StepPayload (dataclass/TypedDict) with from_journal(entry). Public run/ events/resume signatures unchanged.

Command/Strategy for effects: replace the _run_effect if/elif ladder + the separate _kind_for_action map + the _replay_effect ladder with a dict[ActionKind, EffectHandler] (run/replay) and one ActionKind->StepKind table. A new verb becomes one registration instead of edits in five places. Journal payloads + terminal semantics identical.

Extract the ~65-line per-step body of run() into `_advance(...) -> StepOutcome` (Continue | Terminate(state,reason) | EnterRepair) so each transition is unit-testable and the state machine is data, not control flow. run() stays a thin loop; public contract preserved.

_do_rename builds a FULL fresh IndexBuilder().build() on every rename step inside the loop, re-parsing the whole repo, though self._retrieval already holds the cached index for this snapshot. Resolve affected files via the cached index; move the import to module top. Same file set, no IO change.

Replace build_model_gateway's if/elif with a dict[BackendChoice, Callable[[Settings], ModelBackend]] registry; keep the SDK import lazy inside the claude factory so the stub path stays keyless. Signature/return unchanged. (Same registry idea for build_sandbox_client.)

The trust-boundary system prompt exists twice with DIVERGENT text and one copy OMITS the `rename` verb though the parser allows it. Derive the system text and the verb list from a single constant generated from ActionKind (', '.join(k.value ...)); both consumers read it. Wire format unchanged. Security-critical — dedupe so the model's allowlist claim can never drift from the parser's.

Redaction depends on regex ordering + a 3-name allow-list, and _SECRET_VALUE stops at whitespace so multi-line PEM keys / spaced secrets are only partially redacted. Add explicit rules for PEM BEGIN/END blocks and long base64 runs; make _RULES injectable (default preserved); replace the in-loop nonlocal-count closure with a pure substitution fn. RedactionResult + marker format (idempotence/determinism) preserved.

dashboard_summary is O(tasks x steps) N+1 (a get_trace per task) AND uses the default list limit=100, so tasks_total/total_cost silently undercount a user with >100 tasks while being named "total". Push aggregation into SQL (JournalRepo.count_by_kind via JOIN..GROUP BY; a metering SUM/COUNT over ALL the user's tasks). JSON keys unchanged; values become truthful.

create_app does side-effecting IO at call time and builds the sandbox client TWICE; worse, module-level `app = create_app()` runs all of it at import. Build the sandbox once and share it (readyz == orchestrator, as the comment already claims); move the module-level app behind uvicorn `--factory` or guard it so import is IO-free.

JournalRepo.append reads back with get_step() OUTSIDE the write txn (the resume substrate — a subtle interleave undermines effectively-once). Do the read-back INSIDE the immediate() block. Also stop `create()` returning `self.get(...) # type: ignore` (Optional cast to non-None); read back within the same txn or raise. Tuple/return shapes preserved.

DockerSandboxRunner.verify() raises the builtin NotImplementedError, which the ACPError handler will NOT map — leaks a 500 + stack trace. Raise NotImplementedInPhase (like the stub) or implement it. One-line, interface preserved.

The zip path calls extractall() after a pre-scan but does not defend zip symlink members or decompression-ratio (zip-bomb) — weaker than the tar path's filter='data'. Reject symlink members and cap total uncompressed size. Legitimate-archive behavior unchanged.

get_status duplicates TaskStatus construction (with a divergent step_index semantic and no dry_run patch) already done in AgentLoop._status. Extract one TaskStatus.from_task(...) factory both call. Wire shape unchanged.

assert_owned() is defense-in-depth but never wired; triggers block UPDATE on journal/budget_ledger but not DELETE. Either add guarded BEFORE DELETE triggers (allow the tasks ON DELETE CASCADE path, abort ad-hoc deletes) or at minimum wire assert_owned() into the one unscoped getter (get_for_resume) that crosses the trust boundary. No public API change.

low_and_patterns.fix: definitions()/references_of() flatten+sort ALL symbols/refs per call (hot path + rename). Build lazy name->symbols / name->refs maps behind the same methods, invalidated on put_file/drop_file. Sort/serialize determinism preserved.

Object-graph wiring (Settings->Database->Repos->Services->Sandbox->Model) is assembled ad hoc in >=3 modules and drifts (cli calls init_db, gateway assumes it done). Add one acp.bootstrap composition root (build_database/build_workspace_service/build_orchestrator) consumed by BOTH cli and app. Entrypoint signatures unchanged.

Introduce BaseRepo(db) with _fetchone/_fetchall/_write helpers (single seam for the B-CRIT-1 connection fix) and give Database __enter__/__exit__ so CLI/tests close connections deterministically. Additive; names/returns preserved. Also dedupe the copy-pasted `_get_db(request)` into one gateway/deps.py, and the two task->dict serializers into one projection.
_Row.from_row does cls(**dict(row)); a new schema column breaks all reads. Add model_config = ConfigDict(extra='ignore') (or document strict parity).

Keep constant-time compare; optionally add a server-side pepper (HMAC- SHA256 with a settings secret) so a DB-only leak yields nothing. Do NOT switch to bcrypt/argon2 for high-entropy random tokens. Interface-preserving.

workstream.oracle: Full suite green after EACH fix (no regression). B-CRIT-1 proven by a new concurrency test that drives N concurrent write requests and asserts no "transaction within a transaction" / no lost write (fails on the shared connection, passes after). B-3 proven by a concurrent-retrieval test that asserts the budget ceiling is never overshot. B-6 proven by a crash-between-copy-and-head test asserting head/FS stay consistent and a re-commit raises ConflictError. B-13 proven by a test asserting the system prompt's verb list equals {k.value for k in ActionKind}. ruff + mypy clean. No public route/CLI/schema diff (assert the OpenAPI JSON and CLI --help are unchanged before/after). Every interface-affecting item (B-4a) is an explicit, recorded decision.

workstream.name: Comprehensive test suite — 11 layers + coverage gates
workstream.intent: Extend the existing pyramid (unit/integration/smoke + eval) to the full taxonomy and wire an enforced coverage gate. Every hard requirement and adversarial scenario must have a test that would FAIL if the mechanism were removed. Prefer real mechanism assertions over proxies.

coverage_tooling.d: Add pytest-cov to pyproject with `--cov=src/acp --cov-report=term-missing --cov-fail-under=85`; mark the critical-path packages (orchestrator, db, retrieval, gateway) for a 90% sub-target. Wire `make test` to run with coverage and `make test-coverage` to emit the report. CI-style gate: the suite fails below threshold.

layers.layer: Fill gaps exposed by workstream B: the extracted _advance/StepOutcome state transitions, StepPayload.from_journal, the EffectHandler registry, ResultParser kill-classification (per-runner markers), redaction rule table incl. PEM/base64, the cost function, LedgerRepo.charge_atomic and committed_step_indices. Every common/ util (errors mapping, security hash/verify/split_token, logging context, types enums) unit-covered.
Keep existing index->task->verified E2E; add cross-module: retrieval budget shared with loop; workspace worktree isolation under the fixed connection model; dashboard aggregates vs raw repo truth.

End-to-end business workflows against the sample repo through the PUBLIC API only: happy single-file change; self-repair recovery; multi-file rename hitting every call site; dry_run returns a patch without applying; budget-exhaustion clean stop with partial report. Assert terminal state + journal shape, not internal calls.

Snapshot-assert the OpenAPI schema for every /v1 route (status codes, request/response models) so an accidental contract change fails the build. Assert error bodies are the structured {error: code} form and carry x-request-id. This layer also guards workstream B's "no IO change".

Latency/throughput smoke with SLA assertions: p50/p95 for a stub-mode task run; concurrent-task throughput (N parallel submits) proving the connection fix; retrieval hot-path after the index-map fix (B-23); assert no O(repo) re-index on rename (B-11). Keep them fast + deterministic (stub model), gated so they can run in CI.

Authn/authz: no key -> 401; malformed token -> 401; per-key rate limit trips. Injection: the planted adversarial instruction in the sample repo never becomes a command (differential byte-identical-journal proof). Secret-exfil: planted .env secret never appears in retrieval output, model prompt, or sandbox egress; PEM/multiline secret redacted (B-14). Path-traversal: worktree edit escape rejected; zip/tar slip + symlink rejected (B-19). Sandbox: network call fails closed; wall-clock kill; (document, and test where feasible, OOM/pids).
Keep /healthz /readyz; add a post-deploy smoke that `make up` boots keyless and a trivial task reaches a terminal state.

Budget boundaries: exactly-at-limit, zero budget, 1-token budget, step budget of 0. Resume/replay: kill between journal-append and ledger-commit (assert charged exactly once); double-resume of a terminal task is a no-op; resume rebuilds the data channel incl. failure spans. Concurrent worktree clobber -> ConflictError, never silent overwrite. Model I/O: malformed XML, empty content (refusal), truncated (max_tokens) each surface a distinct typed error (B-1/B-2). Repo shapes: empty repo, a repo with no test suite, unicode/space filenames, non-UTF-8 file, very large file span read (B: bounded read). Name-collision symbol across Python+TS for rename.

User A cannot read/trace/aggregate user B's tasks (404 NotFound, existence not leaked) on EVERY /v1 and /v1/dashboard route; user_id is derived only from the key, never from body/header (attempt to forge is ignored). After workstream D: assert NO /v1 route and the published consumer port expose any cross-tenant path — the admin plane is unreachable from the consumer surface.

Config-swap behavior: SANDBOX_RUNNER=python|go|rust|ts each pass the SAME Phase-3 oracle (parity); MODEL_BACKEND=stub never imports the SDK and is deterministic; the admin console honors its enable flag / separate mount. If workstream D adds runtime feature flags, test toggle + audit-row.

workstream.oracle: `make test` runs with coverage and fails under 85% overall / 90% on critical packages; pass rate >=98%. Every §2 hard requirement and §3 adversarial scenario maps to at least one named test (a traceability table in the test docs). Each workstream-A bug fix has a regression test. The full matrix of SANDBOX_RUNNER values passes the shared sandbox oracle.

workstream.name: Superuser admin console — separate realm, read-mostly, audited
workstream.intent: Provide a Django-admin-style master console for a single superuser that surfaces the OpenAPI contract, billing/metering, logs, DB tables, health, and feature metrics/flags in ONE view — WITHOUT breaching consumer isolation. The current /dashboard is an unprivileged, user-scoped consumer and MUST stay that way; the admin plane is a distinct, privileged operator surface.

architecture_rules.r: SEPARATE AUTH REALM: HTTP Basic (or a signed short-TTL session cookie), require_superuser dependency, entirely distinct from require_auth. A tenant API key can NEVER escalate to admin. No is_admin flag bolted onto the users/api_keys tables.

SEPARATE MOUNT / NON-PUBLISHED PORT: mount as a sub-app (e.g. /__admin) whose routes are NOT in the public router set, or run as a separate ASGI process bound to a loopback/ops-only port — never on the single published gateway consumer port. It must be architecturally impossible to reach an admin route from a /v1 path or the consumer port.

READ-MOSTLY over already-emitted data (tasks, journal, budget_ledger, api_keys METADATA). The admin NEVER invokes the agent brain and NEVER opens a new path into the index/sandbox/model. The ONLY write is an audited feature-flag toggle (if D6 is built).

CREDENTIAL HONESTY: the hardcoded ann/123 is DEMO-ONLY. Source it from settings (ACP_ADMIN_USER / ACP_ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH via the existing hash_secret) with a LOUD startup warning when it equals the demo default. Never ship a literal ann/123 in code as a real superuser.

deliverables.d: Health tile: render /healthz + /readyz checks{} (database, sandbox) + model_backend/env from settings. Lowest risk — build first.
Serve the admin sub-app's own Swagger (get_swagger_ui_html) behind require_superuser; render the PUBLIC contract read-only via app.openapi() in an iframe/pre. Do not widen the public /docs.

Cross-tenant billing rollup: add LedgerRepo.committed_cost_usd(scope) + list_ledger(scope), UsersRepo.list(), admin-only TasksRepo.list_all()/ApiKeysRepo.list_all() (metadata, NO key_hash). Show $/task, $/user, $/day, budget-vs-consumed. Uses the unified cost fn from B-7. These cross-tenant queries live ONLY on the admin realm.

Log browser: a logging.Handler mirroring the last N JSON lines into an in-memory ring buffer on app.state, exposed at an admin-only GET; annotate it is process-local (docker logs are the durable source). Never re-introduce secrets; keep redaction discipline.

Read-only DB browser: GET /__admin/db/{table} where {table} is validated against a FIXED allowlist (query built from a constant map — never string-interpolated), SELECT-only with LIMIT/OFFSET, and a column-redaction map that strips key_hash. This deliberately bypasses tenant scoping — document why it must live in the separate realm.

Surface /metrics and effective Settings read-only. If runtime flags are wanted, add a feature_flags table + FlagsRepo (get_all/set) with an admin-only, audit-logged toggle — the sole admin write. Document the departure from the stateless-dashboard philosophy.

workstream.oracle: (1) A tenant API key on any admin route -> 401/403 (no escalation). (2) The published consumer port exposes ZERO admin routes and ZERO cross-tenant path (grep the public router set + an HTTP test hitting the consumer port for /__admin -> not found). (3) The existing /v1 isolation tests still pass unchanged (user A cannot see user B). (4) No admin view ever returns key_hash or a secret (assert on responses). (5) Every admin request writes an audit row. (6) DB browser rejects a non-allowlisted table and cannot be SQL-injected. (7) Superuser auth works with the settings- sourced credential and warns on the demo default. (8) `make up` still boots keyless; the admin plane is opt-in and never blocks the consumer path.
workstream.docs: DESIGN.md gains an "Operator/Admin plane" subsection stating the privileged surface honestly: separate realm + separate port + read-mostly + audit, WHY it does not violate the consumer API-only/isolation invariant, and the explicit tradeoff (a declared, contained exception, not a silent breach). Update the route inventory and the API-only boundary proof.

workstream.name: Rewrite DESIGN.md for a forward-deployed engineer
workstream.intent: Keep the strong existing content (retrieval-vs-RAG, agent loop, sandbox, trust boundary, effectively-once) and restructure into an FDE-friendly doc where every assignment requirement is provably fulfilled and the missing FDE sections are added. Fix the contradictions from workstream A first.

required_sections.s: Executive requirement-coverage matrix at the TOP: one row per assignment requirement (not just the internal 8) — req | mechanism | proof (test file) | quantified status (e.g. "5/5 eval, N/N tests"). Bidirectional traceability: assert every ask maps to >=1 row.
